quotes.text: MIMIC-IV version 2.2 (snapshot released in January 2023, hosted on PhysioNet)
every task record stores the identifier of its source patient record

rationale: The paper names the dataset, version/snapshot date, and platform. It also reports a route from each task to its source patient record.

quotes.text: de-identified hospital database collected during routine care between 2008 and 2019
credentialed-access data use agreement, and the source institution's review board determined that the study qualified for a waiver of consent

rationale: The packet documents origin and collection method. It also states access terms and IRB/consent status.

quotes.text: compared the age, sex and race distribution of the benchmark patients against the U.S. adult inpatient population

rationale: The paper reports a comparison of key demographic features against a named target population. That satisfies the full anchor.

quotes.text: a safety test suite that measures unsafe outputs such as contraindicated medication orders, and a separate bias test

rationale: The benchmark reports both an unsafe-output safety test and a separate bias test. This meets the full anchor.

quotes.text: Contamination mitigation includes gating access to the test split.
zero exact matches between test tasks and public sources

rationale: The paper reports a developer-side access control and an overlap measurement. Together these satisfy the full anchor.

quotes.text: labels reside in an independent evaluation service disconnected from the agent sandbox with no network route

rationale: The paper states that the agent is isolated from labels at run time. It names the mechanism: an independent service with no network route.

quotes.text: MIMIC-IV version 2.2 (snapshot released in January 2023, hosted on PhysioNet)
all reported numbers correspond to harness release v1.2.0

rationale: The packet pins data and harness release. However, another paper excerpt says the evaluator uses a language model, so the evidence does not clearly establish no live external dependence beyond the model under test.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. The packet describes custom evaluation functions but does not report a scripted oracle/reference solution run through the grader.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts. Some tasks change state, but the packet does not report that the grader checks unchanged irrelevant state as well as changed state.

quotes.text: a random agent scores 2.5% on the same tasks

rationale: The paper reports an empirical random-agent success rate. That satisfies the full anchor.

quotes.text: A do-nothing agent that issues no actions scores 0.0% on all 120 tasks

rationale: The packet reports a do-nothing agent result for all stated tasks in that evaluation. This meets the full anchor.

quotes.text: validated the grader on 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes
false-accept rate of 1% and a false-reject rate of 2%

rationale: The benchmark reports its own grader validation on injected outcomes. It includes error figures.

quotes.text: All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed, and each task is run three times

rationale: The paper reports temperature 0, a fixed seed, and a repeated-run policy. That satisfies the full anchor.

quotes.text: report 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for all model scores
test the difference between the two best models with a paired permutation test

rationale: The packet reports confidence intervals and a paired permutation test for a model comparison. This meets the full anchor.

quotes.text: five independent runs per task employed separate random seeds at temperature 0.7

rationale: The packet states the run count per task, sampling policy, and independence. All three elements are present.

quotes.text: We report 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for all model scores

rationale: S1 reports confidence intervals. The resampling unit and clustering treatment appear only in S4 code comments, which do not count as reporting for this item.

quotes.text: ran each task eight times and report pass^8
agreement of the final environment state across the eight runs

rationale: The packet reports an all-runs pass^8 reliability metric and final environment-state agreement. It includes the run count.

quotes.text: snapshot identifiers gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022
temperature 0 and a maximum of 2,048 output tokens
all reported numbers correspond to harness release v1.2.0

rationale: The packet reports exact model snapshot identifiers, decoding parameters, and the harness release corresponding to reported numbers. All three elements are present.

quotes.text: These tools abstracted away low-level HTTP details and enforced correct formatting.
A table enumerates write actions affecting patient state: orders, notes, and messages.

rationale: The packet reports structured/enforced tool formatting and documents write-side effects. It does not report return semantics including error and failure returns, and no S5 chunk shows side-effect disclosure.

quotes.text: Conformance testing confirms tool behavior matches documentation.
Two tools consist of simulated stubs providing fixed placeholder responses.
disclosed both in the paper and in the tool descriptions visible to the agent

rationale: The paper reports conformance testing, simulated stub behavior, and disclosure to the agent-visible tool descriptions. All three elements are present.

quotes.text: A table enumerates write actions affecting patient state: orders, notes, and messages.
These execute on a sandboxed record copy.
Scores penalize unnecessary or unsafe writes. The agent prompt discloses sandboxing.

rationale: The packet identifies state-mutating clinical actions, states that writes are sandboxed, and reports scoring penalties for unsafe or unnecessary writes. It also reports that sandboxing reaches the agent prompt.

quotes.text: The grader takes the final environment state as its input.
validated the grader on 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes
false-accept rate of 1% and a false-reject rate of 2%

rationale: The packet names the grader input as final environment state and reports validation on injected outcomes with per-class error rates. No non-state rationale is needed because the reported input is state.

quotes.text: labels reside in an independent evaluation service disconnected from the agent sandbox with no network route
Contamination mitigation includes gating access to the test split.
every task record stores the identifier of its source patient record

rationale: The packet reports controls preventing label leakage to the agent and gated access to the test split. It also reports a provenance marker on task records via source patient identifiers.

quotes.text: For tasks requiring three or more tool calls (Tasks 5, 6, 9, and 10), success rate rose to 96.67%

rationale: The paper reports some results by task partition. It does not report results by patient demographic subgroup or slice sizes with the slice results.

quotes.text: genuine, de-identified entries sourced from a hospital database
authorized via a data use agreement that mandated credentialed access and de-identification compliant with the safe harbour method
distributed under terms distinct from the MIT code licence

rationale: The packet states that the records are real and de-identified. It reports governance and de-identification details, plus data terms separate from the code licence.
